reasons.D: Closest movement: short clipped sentences and fragments-in-spirit ('Here was his shop. Here... was he.'), dashes, and a gushing piled-up beard description that echo the passage's breathless rhythm, though the editorial 'we' is off.
reasons.B: First person and short declaratives ('I expected a shop.' 'I was.') come near the passage's plain movement, but the dry, knowing irony is cooler and more modern than the author's earnest, gee-whiz delight.
reasons.C: First person, but long balanced periodic sentences, semicolons and polished Jamesian urbanity are far from the passage's fragmented, colloquial enthusiasm.
reasons.A: Editorial 'we', measured formal clauses, semicolons and restrained essayist decorum ('I shall not attempt to describe') have none of the passage's fragments, exclamations or folksy diction.
